content: Sulfathiazole is an organosulfur compound that functions as a short-acting sulfa drug. It is classified as an organic compound. Historically, it was widely used both orally and topically as an antimicrobial agent. However, its use has significantly declined due to the development of less toxic alternatives. Despite this, sulfathiazole is still occasionally utilized, sometimes in combination with other sulfa drugs such as sulfabenzamide and sulfacetamide. It is also used in aquarium treatments. The compound exists in various polymorphic forms, with the imide tautomer being the predominant form, at least in the solid state. In this tautomeric form, the proton is located on the nitrogen atom of the ring, rather than the structure commonly depicted. Sulfathiazole is referenced in several cultural works. It is mentioned in chapter 104 of Kurt Vonnegut's novel Cat's Cradle and in his New Dictionary as well as in some of his short stories. The 1946 novel Mister Roberts by Thomas Heggen describes its use in the treatment of gonorrhea. Additionally, Sonya Dorman's 1966 short story When I Was Miss Dow includes a reference to sulfathiazole. The 1998 movie Dead Heat also mentions the compound, describing it as a drug used in the reanimation of dead bodies. Furthermore, sulfathiazole is noted in John Irving's The World According to Garp in chapter 1, where Garp's mother observes it being dispensed to soldiers during World War II.
